purpose: Voclosporin is used to treat lupus nephritis, which is a type of kidney inflammation caused by lupus. It helps protect your kidneys from damage caused by your immune system attacking them. It is used together with other medicines to get the best results.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes mistakenly attacks your own kidneys when you have lupus nephritis. Voclosporin works by calming down certain immune cells so they stop causing damage to your kidneys. Think of it like a volume control that turns down the overactive part of your immune system that is causing the problem.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include decreased kidney function, high blood pressure, headache, diarrhea, nausea, anemia (low red blood cells), urinary tract infections, tremor or shaking, abnormal kidney lab values, and low magnesium or potassium levels. Let your doctor know if any of these bother you.
warnings: This medicine lowers your immune defenses, so you may be more likely to get serious infections, including bacterial, viral, and fungal infections. It can also affect your kidneys and blood pressure, so regular lab tests and blood pressure checks are very important. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine as it can raise drug levels in your body. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as many drugs can interact with voclosporin. Do not use if you are pregnant unless your doctor specifically says it is necessary.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 23.7 mg (three capsules) taken twice a day, about 12 hours apart. It is best taken consistently either with food or without food each time. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your kidney function and lab results. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
